children: By Niket Nishant, Purvi Agarwal and Ragini Mathur
US stock index futures rebounded sharply on Monday as investors returned to AI-linked shares after last week's drubbing pushed the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory.

The advance follows a tumultuous week for the AI trade, which was already strained by concerns over hefty spending commitments and the durability of demand. Pressure intensified after the abrupt departure of Nvidia
CEO  Jensen Huang and growing worries that AI-related spending could slow after the US midterm elections.
Sentiment was further soured when Anthropic
quickly lost momentum following its highly anticipated market debut on Thursday. Its shares rose 3.4% in premarket trading on Monday, after falling 8.5% on Friday.

"What began in October as a textbook rotation out of Tech from extended levels has morphed into a broader risk-off move amid a succession of negative catalysts," Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note, while adding, "A lot of bad news is already being priced."
But analysts were reluctant to call a recovery yet, despite investors buying into beaten-down valuations.

"Investors appear willing to buy into the recent weakness, but it remains too early to determine whether this marks a sustainable recovery," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.
The S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
and the Dow Jones Industrial Average
both confirmed corrections on Friday, closing more than 10% below their record highs.
The Nasdaq
was down 18% from its peak, while the Nasdaq-100
was just shy of confirming bear-market territory, down 19.8% from its October 6 closing high.
At 7:01 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 971 points, or 2.01%, and S&P 500 E-minis
were up 192 points, or 2.77%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis
were up 862.75 points, or 3.43%.
Chip stocks led Monday's rebound. Nvidia rose 8%, rebounding from its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Advanced Micro Devices
and Broadcom
gained 4.5% and 5.4%, respectively, while Micron Technology
rose 5.3%.
Neocloud and data-center companies also climbed. CoreWeave
rose 7.4%, IREN
gained 8%, Nebius
advanced 9.4%, Applied Digital
added 8.3%, and Core Scientific
rose 6.6%.
Later in the day, investors will assess the S&P Global November Composite PMI for a read on business activity.
The key release this week, however, will be Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could offer fresh direction on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.
Traders are pricing in about a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Recent hawkish signals from policymakers and minutes from the central bank's latest meeting have weighed on sentiment. New York Fed President John Williams is scheduled to speak later on Monday.
Elsewhere, Zscaler
jumped 16% after CrowdStrike
said on Monday it would buy the cybersecurity provider in an all-stock deal that values Zscaler at about $43.9 billion.
CrowdStrike shares fell 8.2%.
